history.summary: A $1.4M 2BR penthouse (1,066 sqft, $1,313 psf) in a 582-unit 2016 leasehold project 390m from Tanah Merah MRT interchange. The ask is the cheapest of ~16 competing penthouses in the project and rents well (~4% gross yield), but Urban Vista's resale prices have been essentially flat for 3 years (1.1% total, 0.96% over the last 12 months) — the MRT premium is fully priced in, and a penthouse with a large outdoor terrace is a niche exit unit at a price point $300-450k above the project's standard 2BRs.
history.rating_rationale: For a 5-7yr investment hold, appreciation is the dominant factor and the data is unambiguous: URA resale CAGR of just 2.2%/yr over 5 years (193 resale transactions, confidence 1.0), decelerating to ~1%/yr in the last 1-3 years — below the D16/OCR baseline of 3.7% and far below RCR's ~5.8%. Base-case projected total return is 3.17%/yr annualized (downside 1.69%) — bond-like returns for equity-like risk. The penthouse format compounds exit risk: ~16 similar PH units in one project, interior space well below the headline 1,066 sqft (large terrace), top-floor heat, and at $1.4M the resale buyer will compare against the project's standard 2BRs at $950k-1.1M and against brand-new Sceneca Residence next door (TOP Dec 2027) with direct MRT/mall integration. The $1,313 psf 'discount' vs the project's $1,554 average is structural penthouse pricing, not a bargain.
red_flags: Flat appreciation: +1.1% total over 3 years, +0.96% over 12 months (URA resale data, 193 txns) despite the east-side market rally
Penthouse niche: large low-value terrace inflates sqft; ~16 competing PH units (1,012-1,163 sqft) in the same project; two near-identical units asking $1.5M signal a crowded exit
Sceneca Residence (268 units + retail, integrated with Tanah Merah MRT) TOPs Dec 2027 — construction noise until then, newer competing stock at resale time
Resident-reported maintenance decay: broken tiles, unrepaired pool furniture, rusty gym equipment (Stacked Homes 6-year resident review) — MCST quality risk
Elevated EW-line MRT track noise adjacent to the development
Tenant-heavy, transient resident profile; tight parking
catalysts: Changi T5 + Changi East Industrial Zone/Urban District (2030s) — long-term employment growth for the East
Changi Airport branch conversion to TEL with Tanah Merah as interchange/terminal (~2040 — beyond a 5-7yr hold)
Sceneca's retail podium (21.5k sqft) adds doorstep amenities from 2028
Sustained rental demand from Changi Business Park, Expo, SUTD and airport workforce

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: Genuinely solid. 390m to an MRT interchange serving CBP/Expo/airport employment keeps the tenant pool deep; project yield runs ~4.1%. A near-identical 1,055 sqft 2BR penthouse asks $5,000/mo — achieved rent of ~$4,500-4,800 implies ~3.9-4.1% gross on this ask, above the 2BR condo norm. Caveats: tenants pay for interior space, not terrace, so the premium over a standard 2BR ($3,800-4,200) is modest; top-floor heat and ongoing Sceneca construction (until late 2027) are tenant friction points. The scorer's $3,731 fallback estimate is too low — researched figure used instead.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The weakest pillar, on the most reliable data in this evaluation. URA resale-only CAGR is 2.2%/yr over 5 years and the trend is decelerating: +1.1% over 3 years, +0.96% over 1 year. The project underperformed its own OCR baseline (3.7%) through a strong east-side market — evidence of project-specific drag (track noise, maintenance, investor-heavy small-unit stock). T5 is the credible re-rating story but lands at the very end of a 5-7yr hold at best. No override applied: the 2.2% project-level rate is already in the model, and if anything recent momentum argues it is generous.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Top-floor penthouse; facing not disclosed. Upside: furthest from EW-line track noise, 'city skyline' view claimed. Downside: equatorial roof heat, and west-facing stacks would worsen cooling costs — verify facing and the interior-vs-terrace sqft split (likely ~750-850 sqft interior of the 1,066) before any offer. Within Urban Vista, the better investment units are the standard 592-700 sqft 2BRs at $950k-1.1M: same rental demand at a lower quantum, much deeper exit pool.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_rate_source: URA resale 5yr CAGR for Urban Vista (193 resale transactions, no new-launch bias) — used as-is
